note: High-level reasons a community federates with other servers, or limits or defederates from them (Federation → (De)federation criteria; a card stores [{ id, note }] in federation.criteria). Each item's short is its name on the published card (the full label in its bubble). Two groups: why we federate, and why we limit or defederate. The second mirrors the rule schema's categories (rule_schema.json: behavior, content; each item's ruleType is the rule type it corresponds to), plus how a server is run (security, privacy, moderation). "federate_by_default" is selected automatically when the approach is "Open, with a denylist". Drafted 2026-11-16; accepted by Sohyeon 2026-11-16.

items.label: We federate by default
items.description: We connect with other servers unless there's a reason not to.

items.label: They reach out, and we agree
items.description: Another community asks to federate with us, and we decide together.

items.label: Similar rules and values
items.description: Their rules and values are close to ours.

items.label: Moderators we trust
items.description: We know their moderation team, and they respond when there's a problem.

items.label: A community we already know
items.description: We already have ties with them: shared members, partners, events.

items.label: Bad-faith behavior
items.description: Trolling, personal attacks or deliberate disruption from their members.

items.label: Harassment
items.description: Their members harass, bully or dogpile ours, and it isn't dealt with.

items.label: Hate and discrimination
items.description: Hate speech or discrimination from their members, left in place.

items.label: Impersonation or fake accounts
items.description: Impersonation, sockpuppets or undisclosed bots.

items.label: Spam and platform misuse
items.description: Spam, mass-following or mass-replying, or unsolicited advertising coming from them.

items.label: Sign-ups with no checks
items.description: Anyone can make an account there, so abusive accounts appear faster than they're removed.

items.label: Sensitive media without warnings
items.description: Graphic, disturbing or sexual media posted without content warnings or labels.

items.label: AI-generated media or uncredited work
items.description: AI-generated media, or others' work posted without credit, that our rules don't allow.

items.label: Explicit content we don't allow
items.description: Adult or explicit content beyond what our rules permit.

items.label: Illegal content
items.description: Content that's illegal where we, or our members, are.

items.label: Violence, threats or extremism
items.description: Violent threats, extremist propaganda or content encouraging self-harm.

items.label: Their rules differ too much from ours
items.description: Overall, their rules allow what ours forbid, or leave out what matters to us.

items.label: Moderation absent or unresponsive
items.description: Reports go unanswered, or there's no one to contact.

items.label: Security practices too lax or unclear
items.description: For example, outdated software, unprotected admin accounts, or no stated security practices.

items.label: Privacy practices we can't accept
items.description: For example, they scrape or republish our members' posts, or share their data.

items.label: They host people we've blocked elsewhere
items.description: For example, accounts that moved there to get around our blocks.
